unit.title: Checkpoint practice papers
unit.subject: Science
unit.note: Written by the Atomic teaching team in the format of Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint Science (0893). Not Cambridge papers.

C1.prompt: Which organ excretes each waste product?
In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis happen?
Which word equation shows aerobic respiration?
A plant was kept in the dark for two days, then one leaf was half covered with black paper and the plant placed in sunlight. The leaf was then tested with iodine. Describe and explain the result.
Put these metals in order of reactivity, most reactive first.
An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
Is each a physical or a chemical change?
Complete the table for the reaction hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide.
head: Product 1
Product 2

C1.prompt: Why does powdered marble react faster with acid than marble chips?

options.t: it has a larger surface area

C1.prompt: A car travels 240 m in 12 s. What is its average speed?
Conduction, convection or radiation?

rows.l: Heat reaching Earth from the Sun
A metal spoon getting hot in soup
Warm air rising above a heater

C1.prompt: Two identical lamps are in parallel with a 6 V cell. What is the voltage across each lamp?

What causes day and night on Earth?
Select TWO pieces of evidence that tectonic plates move.

options.t: coastlines of continents that fit together

C1.prompt: Which variable is it? (How does temperature affect how fast sugar dissolves?)

A student says: 'Plants grow taller with more fertiliser.' Plan a fair test to check this idea.
Which is the best way to make results more reliable?

options.t: repeat the measurements and look for anomalies

C1.prompt: Match each nutrient to its use in the body.

rights: carries urine out of the body

Inherited or environmental variation?
What is a covalent bond?
Which salt does each acid make?
Iron is placed in copper sulfate solution. What do you see?

options.t: a brown coating forms and the solution turns green

C2.prompt: A block has a mass of 54 g and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density?

Float or sink in water (density 1.0 g/cm³)?
What happens to the pitch of a sound when its frequency increases?
Why can't sound travel through space?

options.t: there are no particles to pass on the vibrations

C2.prompt: A ball rolls down a slope. Complete the energy table (no energy wasted).
head: Position
Gravitational potential (J)
Kinetic (J)

options.t: a Mars-sized planet collided with the young Earth

options.t: it should always join every point
it shows the overall trend and ignores small random errors

C2.prompt: Select TWO ways to make a measurement more accurate.

options.t: read the scale at eye level
use an instrument with a finer scale
guess between marks without looking closely

options.t: they make the baby a boy
they help the fetus develop healthily

Match the quantity to its unit.
A force of 600 N acts on an area of 3 m². What is the pressure?

options.t: it bends away from the normal
it slows down and bends towards the normal

D1.prompt: Which material is attracted to a magnet?

Weather or climate?

options.t: the Sun's radiation pushes the dust and gas away

Trial 2 (cm)
Trial 3 (cm)
Mean (cm)
